perf.gpu_e2e_gbps_single_card.note: Released batched GPU path, single card, 2.2 GB real web text resident in RAM; includes host materialization of id arrays. Larger-document condition measured at 0.490 GB/s (larger-document reading record).

perf.gpu_kernel_preview_condition.value: Preview, not part of this release: a prototype CUDA kernel sustains about 24.0 GB/s of raw UTF-8 input text on a single NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090 (llama_3_1_8b tokenizer, 11.92 GB OpenWebText corpus resident in host RAM, disk input excluded) - 24.049 GB/s steady state and 23.763 GB/s whole-file wall clock, measured 2026-07-27. The GPU path shipped in this release is a different and slower engine.
perf.gpu_kernel_preview_condition.note: Not a documentation marker: the qualifying sentence the number may not be published without.

perf.gpu_kernel_preview_gbps.note: Steady-state reading 24.049 GB/s, whole-file wall clock 23.763 GB/s. This figure belongs to a prototype kernel that is not part of this release and must be written with the qualifying sentence (perf.gpu_kernel_preview_condition below).

perf.measurement_setup.value: GPU: released batched path, one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell, 2.2 GB of RAM-resident real web text (llama_3_1_8b), UTF-8 bytes / wall clock, host id arrays materialized; reference: the released reference backend (tokenizers 0.22.2) on the same machine (2x AMD EPYC 9115) and identical input, one core, one thread. Same-input pair on larger documents (1.07 GB, avg 180 KB): 0.490 vs 0.003 GB/s.

perf.reference_cpu_gbps.note: Released reference backend (tokenizers 0.22.2), one core, same machine and input as the GPU reading.
